lines.text: An 8-second vertical phone selfie clip, one continuous take, no cuts.
A woman, hair tied back, plain T-shirt, at a kitchen table.
A clear plastic water bottle, white screw cap, label to camera.
Her phone is propped against a mug, front camera on her, both hands free.
First, she leans in and glances at the lens; the sealed bottle sits in front of her.
Then she reaches down; left hand wraps the bottle, right fingers pinch the cap.
Then one short counter-clockwise twist; the cap turns, the bottle stays still.
Then the cap comes free with a click and lifts in her fingers; the water ripples.
Then she raises the open bottle, eyes on it, cap lowered in her right hand.
Then rim to lips, two swallows; the water level drops.
Finally, she lowers the bottle, exhales, glances to the lens and holds still.
In order: grip, one twist, cap free, lift, drink; nothing changes before it is touched.

Her left hand wraps the bottle body in a full grip and holds it still; her right thumb and index finger pinch the cap and turn it once, counter-clockwise, in one short motion. The cap turns while the bottle stays still, label facing the camera.
Throughout, the bottle keeps its size, label and colour; the cap stays in her fingers; the water only drops as she drinks.
The twist has a visible result: the cap releases with a small click, lifts clear in her fingers, and the water inside ripples once.

Her manner is casual and unforced, like a friend on a call; light, easy, unhurried movements; a breath before she reaches, a glance down as the cap turns, eyes back to the lens after the drink; face alive, no fixed smile.
Camera: propped phone, static; wide front camera, deep focus; medium close-up, slightly low angle.
Shot on a recent iPhone front camera, real not cinematic: 30fps, flat HDR tone, deep focus, no bokeh, faint sensor noise, no grade; real skin with visible pores, not smooth or waxy.
